# Migālopajātaka (Ja 381)

**ID:** Ja 381
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Migālopajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Beast-Swiper the Vulture
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja381
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul5.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Migālopajātaka* (Ja 381) is a narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. Set at Jetavana, the frame story involves an unruly monk (*dubbacabhikkhu*) whom the Buddha admonishes by relating an old-world tale of his former existence [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. In the past story, set in Benares during the reign of King Brahmadatta, the Bodhisatta was born as a king of vultures named Aparanna (or Aparannagijjha) living on Mount Gijjhapabbata [Cowell 1897]. His strong and headstrong son, named Migālopa, persistently soared beyond the bounds of other vultures; despite his father's warning in three stanzas (*gāthās*) to turn back when the earth looks like a four-cornered field (*catukkaṇṇaṃ va kedāraṃ*), Migālopa flew into the high, destructive Verambha winds and was torn to pieces [Fausböll 1883; Cowell 1897]. At the conclusion, the Buddha identifies the unruly monk as Migālopa and himself as the father vulture [Cowell 1897].

Scholars note that the theme of an unruly monk formerly born as a high-flying vulture destroyed in fierce upper-atmospheric winds is also shared with the *Gijjhajātaka* (Ja 427) [JIABS 2013]. DharmaNexus records significant internal text reuse between the *Migālopajātaka* and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (7 matches, over 1600 characters) as well as the *Gijjhajātaka* (Ja 427, 3 matches, segments §4.4–7.1 ↔ §7.3–10.1) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches with score ≥10 are registered in the DharmaNexus database [DharmaNexus].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Tatiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a3) (§4.1–6.6 ↔ §2256_2–2266); Gijjhajātaka (Ja 427) (§4.4–7.1 ↔ §7.3–10.1)
